note: v218 / ADR 0029 — THE PRESCREEN, as measured. `general_listener.may_contain_datable` is the deterministic half of the general listener: it never decides what a date IS, only whether there could be one, so that the backstop has something to compare a silent listener against. Every case below is a shape the 2026-08-25 measurement asked for by name, and every table it reads is either an existing table of this repo read BY NAME (`chronology.YEAR_RE`, `chronology.MONTH_NAMES`, `chronology.NUMBER_WORDS`, `cross_dating.AGE_STATEMENT_RES`, `cross_dating.AGE_BAND_AGES`, `recommend_focuses.TIME_PERIOD_PATTERNS`) or one of the four shapes nothing in the repo could see. The NEGATIVE cases are the load-bearing ones: `marry`, `marching`, the modal `may`, `at 19%` and `at 19:30` are the traps the measurement named.

cases.text: I was born in 1952.
cases.note: years 1800-2099, the one pattern `chronology.YEAR_RE`

cases.text: It was 1899 when they came over.
We will be there in 2099.
There were 1200 of them.
cases.note: a four-digit number outside a life's range is not a year

cases.text: Sometime in the 1970s we sold the farm.
cases.note: the decade form — `chronology`'s own decade pattern is anchored and cannot be spliced into prose, so this is that sentence with the anchors off

cases.text: We married in March.
cases.note: month names, word-bounded

cases.text: I hated marching band.
cases.note: `march` inside `marching` must not fire

cases.text: Did they marry in the end?
cases.note: the `mar` abbreviation must not fire inside `marry`

cases.text: We met in May 1979.
cases.note: `May` fires only capitalized and next to a date

cases.text: It was 2 May 1968.
He may have been right about that.
cases.note: the modal verb never fires

cases.text: We may go in the spring.
At 19 I shipped out.
cases.note: an age statement opening a sentence — `cross_dating.AGE_STATEMENT_RES` read through `_sentence_normalized`

cases.text: At 19% interest nobody was buying.
cases.note: the borrowed table's own exclusion: `at N%` is not an age

cases.text: We got there at 19:30.
cases.note: and `at N:MM` is not an age

cases.text: At 19 Elm Street we had a porch.
cases.note: and neither is a house number

cases.text: When I was about five we moved.
cases.note: spelled-out ages, from `chronology.NUMBER_WORDS`

cases.text: We stayed two years.
cases.note: spelled-out small numbers with a unit

cases.text: Three years back we sold the house.
cases.note: `N back` alongside `N ago`, which nothing in the repo read

cases.text: Five years ago I retired.
I was turning forty when it happened.
cases.note: becoming/turning N — the crossing, not the past

cases.text: He became a teenager that summer.
She stayed until she was nine.
cases.note: a THIRD person's age; every borrowed age table is first-person

cases.text: When Ivo was three we moved again.
cases.note: a capitalized name is the subject

cases.text: As a kid I hated it.
cases.note: life-stage phrases with no number in them

cases.text: Growing up we never had much.
That was in high school.
cases.note: the named periods come from `recommend_focuses.TIME_PERIOD_PATTERNS`

cases.text: My twenties were a blur.
The summer after we moved, everything changed.
cases.note: the owner's relative-dates ruling: a moment fixed against another moment is evidence

cases.text: When Ivo was born we were still in the trailer.
Right after we married he enlisted.
The year Mom died the garden went to seed.
I love a good pizza and a long walk.
cases.note: and nothing at all fires on a message with no time in it
an empty message is not a finding
